canonical_question: Why is the average grain size of the as-cast sample (98 μm) slightly different from the optical estimate (nearly 100 μm), and which is considered more accurate?

question_variants.question: Why is the average grain size of the as-cast sample (98 μm) slightly different from the optical estimate (nearly 100 μm), and which is considered more accurate?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text acknowledges that the EBSD average (98 μm) is in line with the optical estimate (nearly 100 μm), implying consistency, though it does not explicitly state which method is 'more accurate'.

answers.answer: The paper states the EBSD analysis result is 'in line with optical images', showing 98 μm versus the optical estimate of nearly 100 μm.
answers.boundary_limitation: The paper does not declare one method as more accurate, only that they are consistent.
evidence_spans: A coarse grain microstructure having BCC/B2 phases was obtained in the as-cast HEA sample.
Only 5 min of straining of sample significantly refined the grain structure from 98 to 1 μm and 0.43 μm for the SFP_400 and SFP_1800 sample, respectively.
The ultrafine-grained samples showed a phase transition from BCC/B2 to FCC structure.

source_evidence_spans: In line with optical images, EBSD analysis also showed coarse grain microstructure for the as-cast alloy with an average grain size of 98 μm.
